title: Lallan's golgappa stall
body: Lallan runs a golgappa stall. He keeps the pani (spiced water) in a cylindrical vessel of radius 10 cm, and the pani stands to a height of 50 cm. A golgappa is a small hollow ball made of wheat, so for estimation we treat each one as a sphere and neglect the thickness of its shell. Lallan never fills a golgappa completely; on average only a part of its volume is filled with pani. To estimate how many golgappas he can serve, we divide the total volume of pani in the vessel by the volume of pani in one golgappa. Two students using different assumptions about the size of a golgappa and how full it is may reach quite different answers, and that is acceptable in a guesstimate as long as the reasoning is sound.
